newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Explosion rocks Lagos as oil tanker burns.
newsitem.headline: Explosion rocks Lagos as oil tanker burns.

text.p: An oil tanker exploded and caught fire in the bay off Lagos on Friday sending hundreds of workers in the city centre rushing from their offices in panic.
A Western diplomat said he could see thick black smoke billowing from the ship. "There is a huge hole in the side of the vessel but it is still floating," he added.

Shipping authorities said the tanker, the Al-Zainab, was empty when fire broke out. It was anchored off the Atlas Cove jetty where vessels ferrying fuel from refineries in southeastern Nigeria usually offload their cargo in Lagos.
"The fire has gone out. We have not yet established if any lives are lost," said a shipping authority official.
Hundreds of workers in the city centre rushed out of their offices in panic, fearing it was another in the series of bomb explosions that have rocked Nigeria's commercial hub in recent months.
"I have never heard such an explosion before," said book seller Simi Sola.
Witnesses said smaller vessels headed to the rescue of the ship. There were no immediate reports of casualties.
Politically-volatile Nigeria has been hit by bomb blasts since December. The most recent hit a mosque in the eastern city of Onitsha, killing five worshippers.
